ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r1.claim: Paired with al-Mursalat, this surah uses divine providence in the heavens and earth to establish Judgment as the necessary end of a purposeful world, rewarding the God-fearing and punishing rebels.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r1.anchor: The basis of arguments is divine providence evident in every single part of the heavens and the earth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r2.claim: The surahs share an affirmative-question style aimed at deniers; each verse reproaches them while believers' glad tidings are understood against the warning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r2.anchor: The discourse begins with questions which can only be answered in the affirmative.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r4.claim: The signs of providence, mercy, wisdom, and power throughout earth and heavens show that humanity is not unchecked or unaccountable; its fixed day of reckoning must arrive.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p132/r4.anchor: A call to reflect on the signs of God’s providence, mercy, wisdom and power

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p142/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p142/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p142/r5.claim: Rain produces grain for people, grass and vegetation for cattle, and luxuriant orchards.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p142/r5.anchor: provide grain for man and grass

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p342#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p342#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p342#5/r1.claim: Qatada explains alfaf as gardens densely intertwined with one another.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p342#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ألفافا ﴾ قال ملتفة بعضها إلى بعض

AKHFASH:v2p564/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p564/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p564/r1.claim: ألفافا has the singular form لف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p382/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p382/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p382/r3.claim: ألفاف is plural of لف, itself a plural of لفّ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p382/r3.anchor: ألفافا جمع لف، ثم جمع لف على ألفاف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says ألفاف has no singular; Abu Hayyan says there is no need for this because the singular لف is established by most lexicographers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ولا واحد له، كالأوزاع والأخياف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r11.claim: The asserted absence of a singular for ألفاف is unnecessary; لف is recorded as its singular and is the majority lexicographers' view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p384#2/r11.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى هذا القول ولا إلى وجاهته، فقد ذكر في المفردات أن مفرده لف

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r1.claim: Alfāf means intertwined and thickly clustered.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda gives laf as the singular of alfāf.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r3.claim: Alternatively, alfāf is a plural of a collective alf or a plural of lifāʾ, which itself has plural laf.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p509/r3.anchor: ويقال: هو جمع الجمع؛ كأن واحده: "ألف" (2) . و "لفاء"؛ وجمعه: "لف"؛ وجمع الجمع: "ألفاف".

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r1.claim: A جنة is a tree-covered garden that conceals the earth; al-Farra distinguishes a palm grove from a vine-bearing firdaws, and the word can also mean the covering trees.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r1.anchor: جمع جنه وهي كل بستان ذي شجر يستر بأشجاره الأرض من الجن وهو الستر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r2.speaker: زهير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r2.claim: A line by Zuhayr uses جنة for the sheltering trees, supporting that lexical sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r2.anchor: وعليه حمل قول زهير + من النواضح تسقى جنة سحقا +

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says ألفاف means intertwined and has no singular, like words for scattered or varied groups.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r3.anchor: أي ملتفة تداخل بعضها ببعض قيل لا واحد له كالأوزاع والأخياف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba analyzes ألفاف as a collective plural based on لفاء; the author considers the plural-of-plurals account unlikely and non-productive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة جمع لف بضم اللام جمع لفاء فهو جمع الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r5.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r5.claim: Al-Kisaʾi takes ألفاف as the plural of لفيف, meaning wrapped, following the pattern فعيل to أفعال.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r5.anchor: وقال الكسائي جمع لفيف بمعنى ملفوف وفعيل يجمع على أفعال كشريف وأشراف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r6.claim: The Kashshaf suggests deriving ألفاف by deleting extra letters from ملتفة; al-Kashf objects that clipped plurals have no comparable pattern, and the author calls it strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r6.anchor: وفي الكشاف لو قيل هو جمع ملتفة بتقدير حذف الزوائد لكان قولا وجيها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r7.speaker: جمهور اللغويين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r7.claim: Most lexicographers treat ألفاف as the regular plural of لف, a descriptive word meaning wrapped.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r7.anchor: وجمهور اللغويين على أنه جمع لف بالكسر وهو صفة مشبهة بمعنى ملفوف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r8.speaker: الحسن بن علي الطوسي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Tusi recites a line with جنة لف as an example.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r8.anchor: وعن صاحب الأقليد أنه قال أنشدني الحسن بن علي الطوسي جنة لف وعيش مغدق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r9.claim: The acts of creation support resurrection through God's power, wisdom and purposes, and the analogy of waking after sleep and bringing plants from earth; the point rebukes denial and mockery.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p11#2/r9.anchor: دلالة على صحة البعث وحقيقته من أوجه ثلاثة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p313#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p313#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p313#2/r2.claim: ألفاف describes gardens thickly entwined with trees; the plural develops from لف to لف to ألفاف.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p313#2/r2.anchor: {وجنات ألفافا} ملتفة بالشجر، واحدها لف وليف، وقيل: هو جمع الجمع

BAYDAWI-FULL:78:14-16/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:14-16/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:14-16/r4.claim: ألفاف describes interwoven gardens; its forms may derive from لف, لفيف, plural لفاء, or be ‘intermixed’ with affixes removed, supported by a poetic line.
BAYDAWI-FULL:78:14-16/r4.anchor: { وجنت ألفافا } ملتفة بعضها ببعض جمع لف كجذع. قال: جنة لف وعيش مغدق

NAHHAS:v5p127/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p127/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p127/r2.claim: Al-fāf may be plural of liff or plural of a plural formed from lifāʾ/alif then alfāf; Abu Jaʿfar prefers the first because exegetes agree gardens are gathered together, implying density.
NAHHAS:v5p127/r2.anchor: قال أبو جعفر قد ذكرنا قول من قال هو جمع لف وقول من قال هو جمع الجمع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r9.claim: Alfāf means gardens whose trees are packed closely together; he derives this from the abundance of water and explains the plural form.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r9.anchor: أي ملتفة الأشجار مجتمعة بعضها إلى بعض من شدة الري

BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r10.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r10.claim: Al-Baghawī reports that alfāf may be a plural of a plural: a garden is lafāʾ, its plural lif, and the plural of lif is alfāf.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r10.anchor: قال البغوي : وقيل : هو جمع الجمع , يقال : جنة لفاء , وجمعها لف بضم اللام , وجمع الجمع ألفاف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r11.claim: The sky, earth, rain, and plants resemble a reproductive pair: sky is male, earth female, water semen, and vegetation their offspring; springs and pools are implied.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r11.anchor: وجعل ذلك أشبه شيء بما يتولد بين الزوجين من الأولاد , فالسماء كالزوج والأرض كالمرأة , والماء كالمني

BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r12.speaker: مقاتل
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r12.claim: Muqātil says every sign just mentioned is more astonishing than resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p297/r12.anchor: قال مقاتل : وكل من هذا الذي ذكر أعجب من البعث

DURR-FULL:v8p392/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the gardens are clustered together.

DURR-FULL:v8p392/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r10.claim: Mujahid says the gardens are intertwined.

DURR-FULL:v8p392/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r11.claim: Qatada says the gardens are interwoven with one another.
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r11.anchor: عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p392/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r12.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r12.claim: Ikrima says crops become gardens when their parts grow close together.
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r12.anchor: عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن عكرمة

DURR-FULL:v8p392/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas also describes gardens whose parts have grown intertwined.
DURR-FULL:v8p392/r13.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3394#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3394#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3394#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the gardens are clustered together.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3394#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : وجنات الفافا قال : مجتمعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p26/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p26/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p26/r4.claim: ‘Gardens’ stands for their trees; the word evokes generous shade, fruit, water, and beauty, while ‘dense’ adds beauty even though farmers may prefer spacing for yield.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p26/r4.anchor: ووجه إيثار لفظ { جنات } أن فيه إيماء إلى إتمام المنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r2.claim: ألفافا can be the plural of لفة, describing branches and leaves intertwined in fresh, well-watered growth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r2.anchor: وألفافا جمع لف بضم اللام، ولف جمع لفاء. والمعنى ملتفات الأغصان والأوراق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r3.speaker: جمهور اللغويين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r3.claim: Most linguists derive ألفافا from لف with kasra, a garden densely wrapped in branches.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r3.anchor: وقال جمهور اللغويين ألفافا جمع لف بكسر اللام، واللف: الجنة الملتفة بالأغصان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r4.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says ألفافا is the plural of لفيف.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r5.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p425/r5.claim: A poet's line uses ألفاف to describe intermingled groups and origins.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7/r1.claim: Alfāf means gardens thickly intertwined with trees; the singular is lafāʾ, the plural lif, and alfāf is a plural of the plural.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7/r1.anchor: أي ملتفة من الشجر ليس بينها خلال الواحدة لفاء وجنات لف وجمع الجمع ألفاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p7/r2.claim: Mention of these created things is evidence for resurrection.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p303#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p303#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p303#2/r4.claim: God uses abundant, beneficial rain to grow grain stored for people and livestock, edible fresh plants, and gardens with varied fruits, colors, flavors, and scents.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p303#2/r4.anchor: أي: لنخرج بهذا الماء الكثير الطيب النافع المبارك {حبا} يدخر للأناسي والأنعام،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p303#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p303#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p303#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain “interwoven gardens” as gardens growing together, comparing their diversity despite shared water to another verse.

SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says ‘alfafan’ means intertwined and has no singular, like ‘awza‘’ and ‘akhyaf’.
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r1.anchor: ألفافا ": ملتفة لا واحد له كالأوزاع والأخياف

SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r2.speaker: أبو علي الطوسي
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r2.claim: Most language authorities analyze ‘alfafan’ as the plural of ‘liff’; Abu ‘Ali al-Tusi’s line ‘jannat liff’ witnesses that form.
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r2.anchor: وأنشد أبو علي الطوسي: 4468 جنة لف وعيش مغدق

SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r3.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r3.claim: Al-Kisa’i analyzes ‘alfafan’ as a plural of ‘lafif’, like sharif/ashraf and shahid/ashhad; a line uses ‘alifaf’ for interwoven groups.
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r3.anchor: الثالث: أنه جمع لفيف، قاله الكسائي. ومثله: شريف وأشراف، وشهيد وأشهاد

SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives the form through pluralization twice: ‘alf’ and ‘lifā’’ first yield ‘liff’, then ‘alfaf’.
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r4.anchor: قاله ابن قتيبة. إلا أن الزمخشري، قال: " وما أظنه واجدا له نظيرا

SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari doubts the double-plural analysis because he knows no parallel such as ‘khudr/akhḍar’ or ‘ḥumr/aḥmar’.
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r5.anchor: وما أظنه واجدا له نظيرا من نحو: خضر وأخضار، وحمر وأحمار

SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r6.claim: The lack of a productive plural-of-plural pattern does not invalidate Ibn Qutayba’s analysis; ‘liff’ resembles ‘qufl’ and can take the pattern ‘af‘al’, while plural-of-plurals need not be regular.
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r6.anchor: لأن جمع الجمع لا ينقاس، ويكفي أن يكون له نظير في المفردات كما رأيت

SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also suggests that ‘alfafan’ could be ‘multaffah’ with its additions removed; the author finds this needlessly strained, since such deletions are chiefly discussed in diminutives and verbal nouns.
SAMIN-DURR:78:16/r7.anchor: ولو قيل: هو جمع ملتفة بتقدير حذف الزوائد لكان قولا وجيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r4.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r4.claim: Alfafa gardens may be crops growing densely beside one another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r4.anchor: أحدها : أنها الزرع المجتمع بعضه إلى جنب بعض ، قاله عكرمة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r5.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r5.claim: They may be trees entwined with fruit.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r6.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r6.claim: They may be gardens containing many colors.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r6.anchor: الثالث : أنها ذات الألوان ، قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r7.claim: Alternatively, crops may cover the ground while trees fill the upper spaces, all growing densely together.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p184/r7.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أنها التي يلف الزرع أرضها والشجر أعاليها ، فيجتمع فيها الزرع والشجر ملتفات .

MUJAHID:v2p720/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p720/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p720/r1.claim: Mujahid says ألفاف means dense and interwoven gardens.
MUJAHID:v2p720/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وجنات ألفافا ﴾ قال يقول جنات ملتفة

MUQATIL:78:11-16/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:78:11-16/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:78:11-16/r6.claim: The gardens are densely interwoven with trees.
MUQATIL:78:11-16/r6.anchor: { وجنات ألفافا } [آية: 16] يعني وبساتين ملتفة بعضها إلى بعض

NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#15/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#15/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#15/r1.claim: Alfāfan means gardens with densely intertwined trees; its singular may be laf, lafīf, absent, or the phrase may be a plural of a plural.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#15/r1.anchor: ملتفة الأشجار واحدها لف كجذع وأجذاع ولفيف كشريف وأشراف

NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#15/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#15/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#15/r2.claim: There is no stopping from “Did We not make” through “thick gardens”; a necessary pause occurs at either “pegs” or “livelihood.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p310#15/r2.anchor: ولا وقف من ألم نجعل إلى ألفافا والوقف الضروري على أوتادا معاشا

QURTUBI-FULL:78:14-15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:14-15/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:78:14-15/r10.claim: Alfaf are gardens whose branches and trees grow closely interwoven; the word has disputed singular forms or may be a plural of a plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:14-15/r10.anchor: أي ملتفة بعضها ببعض لتشعب أغصانها

QURTUBI-FULL:78:14-15/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:14-15/r11.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:78:14-15/r11.claim: Al-Kisa‘i gives liff or luff as singular forms of alfaf; another view treats alfaf as a plural of the plural liff.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:14-15/r11.anchor: وقيل: واحد الألفاف لف بالكسر، ولف بالضم

QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r1.speaker: الأخفش وأبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubayda offer lafif as a singular, like sharif/ashraf.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r1.anchor: وعنه أيضا وأبي عبيدة: لفيف كشريف وأشراف

QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says it would also be sound to treat alfaf as a plural of multaffah after deleting augmentative letters.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r2.anchor: ولو قيل جمع ملتفة بتقدير حذف الزوائد لكان وجيها

QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r3.claim: Laffa can describe a dense garden or plant, and laf’a a thick-limbed woman; the syntax may omit “we bring forth” before gardens.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r3.anchor: ونخرج به جنات ألفافا، فحذف لدلالة الكلام عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r4.claim: The interlacing describes closely spaced garden trees whose strong branches grow near one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:78:6-16/r4.anchor: ثم هذا الالتفاف والانضمام معناه أن الأشجار في البساتين تكون متقاربة، فالأغصان

RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r5.claim: All terrestrial growth falls into three exhaustive classes: grain with husks, grasses without husks or stems, and trees that form gardens; 20:54 names the first two.
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r5.anchor: فثبت بالدليل العقلي انحصار ما ينبت في الأرض في هذه الأقسام الثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r6.claim: Grain comes first because it is basic food, plants next because animals need them, and orchards last because fruit is less essential.
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r6.anchor: وإنما قدم الله تعالى الحب لأنه هو الأصل في الغذاء

RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says alfaf has no singular, like awzaʿ and akhyaf.
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r7.anchor: ذكر صاحب الكشاف أنه لا واحد له كالأوزاع والأخياف

RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r8.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Kisaʾi give the singular as lif with kasra; al-Kisaʾi also allows lif with damma.
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r8.anchor: فقال الأخفش والكسائي واحدها لف بالكسر

RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r9.speaker: المبرد
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r9.claim: Al-Mubarrad rejects the damma form and instead proposes lifa as singular, pluralized as lif and then alfaf.
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r9.anchor: وأنكر المبرد الضم ، وقال بل واحدها لفاء وجمعها لف ، وجمع لف ألفاف

RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r10.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r10.claim: Al-Qaffal offers lifif as a possible singular, by analogy with sharif and ashraf; alfaf means closely interwoven gardens.
RAZI-FULL:v31p9/r10.anchor: وقيل : يحتمل أن يكون جمع لفيف كشريف وأشرف نقله القفال رحمه الله

STUDYQURAN:78:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:78:15/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:78:15/r1.claim: God remains the primary cause: rain is the means by which He produces grain, plants, and gardens, since He made every living thing from water.
STUDYQURAN:78:15/r1.anchor: God remains the primary cause for all things. Therefore, it is not the rain that produces grain

ASAD-NOTES:78:12#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:78:12#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:78:12#n8/r1.claim: Nature's evidence of purpose points to a conscious Creator who made nothing without purpose; the sequence anticipates judgment on whether people follow moral standards known through instinct and revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:78:12#n8/r1.anchor: the overwhelming evidence of purpose and plan in all observable nature points to the existence of a conscious Creator

TAB-FULL:v24p16/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p16/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p16/r1.claim: Water produces grains, the seed-bearing kernels enclosed in husks and harvested, like barley grains and dates.
TAB-FULL:v24p16/r1.anchor: تضمنه كمام الزرع التي تحصد، وهي جمع حبة

TAB-FULL:v24p16/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p16/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p16/r2.claim: Nabāt means fodder for grazing, including grasses and crops.
TAB-FULL:v24p16/r2.anchor: وأما النبات فهو الكلأ الذي يرعى، من الحشيش والزروع

TAB-FULL:v24p18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r1.claim: Alfāfan means gardens densely entwined and gathered together; the early interpreters agree on this sense.

TAB-FULL:v24p18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the gardens are gathered together, one intertwined with another.

TAB-FULL:v24p18/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r4.claim: Qatāda says the gardens are intertwined, one beside another.

TAB-FULL:v24p18/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd describes gardens interwoven, some over others.
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r5.anchor: قال: هي الملتفة، بعضها فوق بعض

TAB-FULL:v24p18/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says alfāf is the plural of liff or lafīf, because interpreters agree it means intertwined; lafāʾ means thick, which does not itself imply intertwining except by interpreting it as density from entanglement.
TAB-FULL:v24p18/r6.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أن الألفاف جمع لف أو لفيف، وذلك أن أهل التأويل مجمعون على أن معناه: ملتفة

TABATABAI:78:9-16/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:9-16/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:78:9-16/r13.claim: “Interwoven gardens” is coordinated with grain; their trees are densely entwined with one another.
TABATABAI:78:9-16/r13.anchor: وجنات ألفاف أي ملتفة أشجارها بعضها ببعض

TABATABAI:78:9-16/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:78:9-16/r14.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:78:9-16/r14.claim: Some say alfāf is a plural with no singular form from the same word.
TABATABAI:78:9-16/r14.anchor: قيل إن الألفاف جمع لا واحد له من لفظه

TABRISI:78:2-16/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:78:2-16/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:78:2-16/r21.claim: The gardens are orchards dense with trees; “trees of” is omitted because the context makes it clear.
TABRISI:78:2-16/r21.anchor: أي بساتين ملتفة بالشجر والتقدير ونخرج به شجر جنات ألفافا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r1.claim: Alfaf describes gardens whose trees are intertwined with no open space between them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: ملتفة من الشجر، ليس بينها خلال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r2.claim: They give the singular of alfaf as lif with kasra; al-Kisaʾi also allows lif with damma.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r2.anchor: قال الأخفش (¬6)، والكسائي (¬7): واحدها: (لف) بالكسر، وزاد الكسائي: (لف) بالضم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r3.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r3.claim: He rejects lif with kasra as unattested; the singular is lifaʾ, its plural lif, and the plural of lif is alfaf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r3.anchor: وأنكر أبو العباس الكسر، وقال: لم يسمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r4.claim: They describe the gardens as dense with intertwined plants and trees.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون: يعني: بساتين ملتفة النبات والشجر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r5.claim: The gardens show that their creator has power to resurrect the dead.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p124#2/r5.anchor: أعلم الله عز وجل بما خلق أنه قادر على البعث

ELMALILI:78:14-30/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:78:14-30/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:78:14-30/r3.claim: Alfaf is the plural of leff: interwoven, tangled, or embracing gardens.
ELMALILI:78:14-30/r3.anchor: “Leff”in cem‘i, mültef, girift yani sarmaş dolaş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:12/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:12/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:12/r1.claim: The seven firm heavens, sun, rain-bearing clouds, and life-sustaining growth display God's power to create a new realm, the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:78:12/r1.anchor: Gökleri, alev alev yanarak dünyayı aydınlatan güneşi, bolca yağmur indirerek yeryüzünde birçok nimetin yetişmesine ve hayatın devam etmesine vesile olan bulutları yaratan yüce kudret

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p415/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p415/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p415/r3.claim: The form is unique in the Quran; its root also appears in al-ʿAsr, Yusuf’s dream and the harvest year, and the whirlwind in al-Baqara.

ITQAN:v2p566/r34.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r34.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r34.claim: ألفافا is the plural of لف, with kasra on the first consonant.
